skills.when_to_use: Use when reading or writing Notion pages, databases, markdown, file uploads, or Workers via the ntn CLI or the Notion API (curl).

skills.name: pdf
skills.description: Create, read, merge, fill, and secure PDF files. Use when generating PDFs, extracting text/tables, building or filling AcroForm forms, merging/splitting/watermarking/stamping pages, encrypting or decrypting documents, or preparing official IRS tax forms.
skills.when_to_use: Use when generating reports/invoices as PDF, building or filling AcroForm forms (with layout linting and visual overlays), extracting text, tables, metadata, or form-field values, merging/splitting/rotating/watermarking/stamping pages, exporting pages as PNGs for visual review or OCR hand-off, managing metadata/attachments, or encrypting/decrypting with passwords. NOT for scanned/image-only PDFs (see references/ocr-extraction.md) and NOT for pixel-perfect HTML-to-PDF rendering (use a headless browser).

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions 'deck', 'slides', 'presentation', or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
skills.when_to_use: Use whenever any .pptx file is involved — creating, reading, editing, combining, splitting, or working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments — triggered by 'deck', 'slides', 'presentation', or a .pptx filename. Also use for structured programmatic work on .pptx decks via python-pptx (create from JSON spec, structured read-back, targeted text/chart/image edits, template filling, slide PNG rendering) and the legacy binary .ppt — convert it with `soffice --convert-to pptx old.ppt` first.

skills.name: arxiv
skills.description: Search arXiv papers by keyword, author, category, or ID.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to search arXiv papers by keyword, author, category, or ID, or to fetch a paper's metadata, abstract, or PDF.

skills.name: context7-cli
skills.description: Operates the ctx7 CLI and Context7 MCP registry — resolve a library ID, then query its docs (doc lookup / find-docs), skills install/search/suggest/list/remove/generate, and MCP setup. Use when mentioning ctx7 or context7, looking up API docs or library docs for a library or framework, finding docs via ctx7, installing skills, or configuring Context7 MCP for an editor.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user mentions ctx7, context7, or find-docs; asks to look up API docs or library docs for a library or framework; wants docs via MCP (context7__resolve-library-id / context7__query-docs) or the ctx7 CLI; wants to install, search, suggest, list, remove, or generate skills; or needs Context7 MCP set up for Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, or a project.

skills.name: fetch-mcp
skills.description: Scrapes web to markdown with transcripts. Use when extracting articles, HTML, YouTube text, or reformatting YouTube content into chapters, threads, blog posts, or quotes.
skills.when_to_use: Use when reading content from external web pages, blogs, or documentation URLs; converting noisy pages to clean Markdown articles; fetching structured JSON from REST API endpoints; extracting captions/transcripts from YouTube videos; or reformatting YouTube content into chapters, threads, blog posts, or quotes.

skills.name: llm-wiki
skills.description: Karpathy's LLM Wiki: build/query interlinked markdown KB.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to create, build, or start a wiki, ingest a source into a wiki, ask a question about an existing wiki, or lint/audit/health-check a wiki.

skills.name: skill-audit
skills.description: Repairs all sac findings across the skill library, then commits and pushes the result.
skills.when_to_use: Run when the user asks to clear every sac lint violation of the skills pack, make sac lint exit 0, fix all pack lint issues, or repair lint findings and push. Trigger terms: skill audit, lint the pack, fix lint violations, audit skills. Authoring one new skill belongs to skill-create; repairing one skill's body against the ten-question quality gate belongs to skill-improve; consolidating duplicate skill folders into one belongs to skill-prune. This skill audits the skills pack through to a clean lint, a rebuilt catalog, and a push.

skills.name: skill-create
skills.description: Authors a SKILL.md from a job description.
skills.when_to_use: Author a new SKILL.md for a capability that has no loaded skill: answer the ten core questions, draft, write, score, verify. Trigger terms: create skill, new skill, author skill. One skill per invocation; repairing an existing skill belongs to the sibling skill-improve. --dry-run stops after the report without writing.

skills.name: skill-improve
skills.description: Audits and repairs a SKILL.md against lint and quality gates.
skills.when_to_use: Audit and repair an existing skill in one pass: structure, frontmatter, body shape, dangling refs, pattern-B variants, and the quality score gate (ten core questions). Trigger terms: improve skill, audit skill. Accepts one skill, a category tree, the skills root, or an explicit list. Authoring a brand-new skill belongs to the sibling skill-create. --dry-run stops after the report without writing.

skills.name: skill-prune
skills.description: Consolidate duplicate skill folders into one.
skills.when_to_use: Collapse overlapping or duplicate skill folders into one consolidated folder, archiving the dropped ones. --dry-run stops after the report without writing.

skills.name: skill-rename
skills.description: Use to rename a Hermes skill and propagate every reference.
skills.when_to_use: Use when asked to rename a skill, re-slug its folder, or diagnose why a skill's slash command is missing. A skill's frontmatter name IS its slash command, so a rename touches more than the folder.

skills.name: skill-research
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills from the open skills ecosystem: searches by keyword, checks the skills.sh leaderboard, verifies quality before recommending, and presents install options. --improve audits and repairs an existing skill; --prune merges duplicate skills.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks \"how do I do X\" where X might be a common task with an existing skill, says \"find a skill for X\" or \"is there a skill that can...\", asks \"can you do X\" for a specialized capability, or expresses interest in extending agent capabilities.

skills.name: skill-traces
skills.description: Learns from, evolves, and unlearns skills from Grok Build session traces in one pass. --learn creates skills for repeated hand-typed instructions and open gaps; --evolve fixes stale lines in loaded skills; --unlearn retires skills the traces show are never used. Deterministic counts and repeated-phrase material come from the trace pipeline (usage.json, phrases.json); memory-v2 topics add topic-level learn/stale/unlearn signals and the --unlearn keep-list (memory.json). a narrow window lists but does not retire.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to learn new skills from repeated hand-typed instructions, evolve stale skill lines to match current reality, or retire skills the traces show they never use. Pick one or more modes: --learn, --evolve, --unlearn; the trace pipeline runs once and every mode applies its own action kinds.

skills.name: execute-plan
skills.description: Executes a PR Plan DAG end-to-end: Hermes validates the plan and drops /execute-plan into Grok Build (Grok runs parallel Orca worktrees, implementers, the 5-reviewer panel, fix loops, and final assembly), then Hermes verifies the final branch and ships the PR.
skills.when_to_use: Use for /execute-plan <plan-doc-path> [--resume <PLAN_ID>], execute plan, run the plan, implement the plan, or after /planner (or /plan) produces a PR plan.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: Relentlessly interviews a plan or design until a shared understanding is reached, and writes resolved decisions back into the original plan.
skills.when_to_use: Use when asked to grill, interview, or stress-test a plan, design, or decision tree until every branch is resolved. Triggers: 'grill this plan', 'interview this design', 'stress-test my approach'.

skills.name: implement
skills.description: Run the implement → review → fix loop for a single small-to-medium task in one Orca worktree: Hermes plans the brief, drops /implement into Grok Build (Grok runs the full loop with its 5-reviewer panel), then Hermes verifies, commits, pushes, and opens the PR.
skills.when_to_use: Use when asked to implement, build, add a feature, fix a bug, or via the /implement slash command. Best for tasks that fit in one worktree. For multi-PR stacks with dependencies, use /execute-plan instead.

skills.name: planner
skills.description: Orchestrates a write-review-revise loop using `plan-doc-writer` and `plan-doc-reviewer` subagents to produce a polished plan document and PR plan.
skills.when_to_use: Use when asked to write a plan doc, produce a system architecture/spec, or via the `/planner <description>` slash command. Triggers: 'plan a feature', 'plan a feature', 'write a plan doc', 'create technical spec'.

skills.name: popular-web-designs
skills.description: 54 real design systems (Stripe, Linear, Vercel) as HTML/CSS.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants a page styled like a known site — 'build a page that looks like Stripe/Linear/Vercel', a landing page, dashboard, or UI using a real design system's tokens and components.
